quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 (Jan-Dec 2025) results (annual securities report): net sales JPY 409,670 million (+3.3% YoY), operating income JPY 1,342 million (-96.4% YoY), ordinary loss JPY 3,886 million (prior year: ordinary income JPY 37,457 million), net loss attributable to owners of the parent JPY 11,751 million (prior year: net income JPY 19,877 million); operating margin 0.3%, ROE -2.0%. Management states that the semiconductor market stayed polarized - AI data center demand grew strongly while consumer, industrial and automotive demand stagnated; for 300mm wafers, leading-edge products saw sustained strong demand on increased AI chip production while non-leading-edge products recovered only gradually under customer inventory adjustment, and 200mm and smaller shipments stayed weak all year. Depreciation rose with the capex executed to expand leading-edge 300mm capacity. Single segment (high-purity silicon).
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 net sales JPY 409,670 million (+3.3%); operating income JPY 1,342 million (-96.4%); net loss JPY 11,751 million

quarterly_data.signal: Major customer (annual securities report, sales by principal counterparty): Sumitomo Corporation accounted for JPY 110,600 million, 27.0% of FY2025 net sales (FY2024: JPY 98,193 million, 24.8%).
quarterly_data.figure: Customer Sumitomo Corporation: JPY 110,600 million, 27.0% of FY2025 net sales (FY2024: 24.8%)

quarterly_data.signal: Production (annual securities report): FY2025 production JPY 355,585 million at manufacturing cost, 109.7% of the prior year. The company does not disclose orders because most of its products are not made to order.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 production JPY 355,585 million (109.7% of prior year)

quarterly_data.signal: Management's outlook and priorities (annual securities report, as of FY2025 year-end): the 300mm wafer market sees strong demand for leading-edge logic and DRAM for AI data centers, and NAND demand is also expected to grow with the expansion of server SSDs; in non-leading-edge logic, customers plan full-scale inventory optimization and purchase volumes are expected to be adjusted. SUMCO is pursuing business structure reform: for 300mm it will bring the new factory up to full capability and upgrade existing plants' equipment to capture fast-growing leading-edge demand; for 200mm and smaller it will reorganize its production system to improve efficiency and earnings.

R&D (annual securities report): FY2025 R&D expenses were JPY 11,151 million, 2.7% of consolidated net sales. The company says the rapid growth of AI products and the move to 3D structures, driven by the limits of device scaling, require major change in silicon wafers; its R&D priorities include joint development of new products with customers (aiming to win the 'first call' for joint development of wafers for next-generation devices), AI-driven productivity gains and faster new-product ramps, more precise evaluation technology, and upgrading existing plants' equipment to handle a rising share of leading-edge products.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 R&D expenses JPY 11,151 million (2.7% of net sales)

quarterly_data.signal: Capex and facilities (annual securities report): FY2025 capex totaled JPY 79,957 million, mainly investment to expand capacity for high-precision wafers for leading-edge 300mm semiconductors. As of December 31, 2025 the company reported no plans for significant new facilities or major renovations. 300mm wafers are made in Imari and Kohoku (Saga), Yonezawa (Yamagata), Omura (Nagasaki) and Taiwan; polysilicon for semiconductors in Yokkaichi (Mie) and the US. Book value of main facilities as of December 31, 2025: Kyushu Imari plant (Saga) JPY 342,182 million; Formosa Sumco (Yunlin, Taiwan) JPY 208,663 million.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 capex JPY 79,957 million; no significant new facility plans as of Dec 31, 2025
